role: Sub-Contractor (49% share under M/s Gurbachan Singh Constructions Pvt. Ltd.)
name: External Road Connectivity — Multi Modal Logistics Park, Jalna (EPC Mode)
gross_value: Rs. 4,16,41,900.79 (revised total contract value, incl. GST)
certifying_signatory: Sanjeev Patil, Chief Executive Officer, Maharashtra MMLP Pvt. Ltd.

showcase.strategic_overview: A landmark engagement within the Government's National Logistics Policy framework, this EPC-mode project delivers the road connectivity backbone for the Jalna Multi Modal Logistics Park (MMLP) — a strategic node in India's integrated logistics ecosystem. As 49% sub-contractor under M/s Gurbachan Singh Constructions, Baltej Infra contributed to infrastructure that will catalyse freight efficiency across Maharashtra's hinterland.
showcase.scope_and_execution: Executed in EPC mode under Maharashtra MMLP Pvt. Ltd. (NHLML/JNPA SPV), the project involved construction of external road connectivity linking MMLP Jalna to the surrounding highway network. Commenced 08 April 2025 and completed by 30 June 2025 — an 83-day delivery cycle — against a revised total contract value of Rs. 4.16 Cr. A 3-year DLP from completion date signals the infrastructure's long-term operational criticality.
showcase.innovation_edge: EPC procurement required integrated design-and-build execution, demanding concurrent engineering and construction management capability. Works were delivered against NHLML and Maharashtra MMLP technical standards, with third-party certification by CEO Sanjeev Patil confirming conformance to specification.
showcase.value_realized: Certified 'Satisfactory' — NIL penalty — by Maharashtra MMLP Pvt. Ltd. CEO. A contribution to national logistics modernisation: the road link directly enables MMLP Jalna's multi-modal freight operations, reducing logistics costs and supporting PM GatiShakti connectivity objectives.

client: SJVN Ltd. — Nathpa Jhakri Hydro Power Station
name: BTRDT Road Strengthening, Drainage & Slope Protection — NJHPS Nathpa

showcase.strategic_overview: Infrastructure delivery at the operating face of one of India's largest hydro-power stations — the 1500 MW Nathpa Jhakri Hydro Power Station. Strengthening the BTRDT road from Check Post to RD 476m, along with drainage, parapets, and slope protection, ensures safe operational access to mission-critical hydro infrastructure in a high-altitude, seismically sensitive environment.
showcase.scope_and_execution: The scope encompassed 476 linear metres of BTRDT road strengthening, integrated drainage channels, safety parapets, and slope protection works — all within the operational perimeter of NJHPS Nathpa. With a 14-month delivery window (Oct 2023 – Dec 2024) under SJVN's stringent in-house engineering oversight, the project demanded continuous coordination with SJVN's O&M and project coordination teams. Execution followed CPWD Specifications and SJVN internal standards.
showcase.innovation_edge: Works within an active power station precinct required meticulous traffic and site management to protect hydro-civil infrastructure from construction-related impact. SJVN's in-house DGM (P&C) provided direct technical oversight, ensuring every intervention was calibrated to operational continuity. Drainage design accounted for the extreme rainfall intensities experienced in the Sutlej River basin.
showcase.value_realized: Certified 'Satisfactory' by SJVN DGM (P&C). Delivered critical access and slope integrity improvements protecting NJHPS Nathpa's operational infrastructure — safeguarding a national energy asset contributing 1500 MW to the northern grid.

name: O&M — Four-Lane Parwanoo–Solan Section NH-22 (NH-5), EPC Mode
certifying_signatory: Authorised Signatory, G R Infraprojects Limited

showcase.strategic_overview: The largest single contract in the Firm's portfolio — Rs. 6.80 Cr — delivering sustained Operation & Maintenance of a 39-km four-lane EPC highway stretch (Km 67.000 to 106.139) on the Parwanoo-Solan section of NH-22. This engagement represents Baltej Infra's graduation into long-cycle highway O&M management, a discipline demanding continuous performance delivery over extended periods.
showcase.scope_and_execution: Nearly two years of continuous highway O&M (Sep 2023 – Jul 2025) across a four-lane divided carriageway in Himachal Pradesh's challenging topography, sub-contracted under G R Infraprojects Limited's NHAI EPC mandate. The Firm managed routine and reactive maintenance, safety compliance, Traffic Management Plans, and quality documentation across the full 39-km operating envelope.
showcase.innovation_edge: Highway O&M at EPC scale demands predictive maintenance systems, real-time defect response, and systematic performance reporting to the Authority Engineer. The Firm maintained continuous quality compliance over the contract period — evidenced by a dual 'Good/Satisfactory' grading — with NIL penalty and NIL arbitration throughout.
showcase.value_realized: Certified 'Good/Satisfactory' by G R Infraprojects Limited. NIL delay penalty. Sustained 39 km of four-lane national highway in operational condition through two complete monsoon cycles, directly protecting road-user safety and freight movement on one of Himachal Pradesh's primary highway corridors.
